<description>
This migrates the headers presync parameters (`commitment_period` and `redownload_buffer_size`) from being precomputed chainparams to being computed at runtime whenever a headers sync starts. This has as advantages:
* Less work for maintainers that need to occasionally run the current `contrib/devtools/headerssync-params.py` script.
* Less room for mistakes in that process.
* Automatically adapts based on time (as opposed to needing to predict the lifetime of the software).

To achieve this, the parameter search algorithm is implemented in C++. It is simpler, because it does not attempt to model the fact that the attacker is forced to submit their headers in batches of 2000 if they want to maintain the attack. The old Python code did that, but actually got it (slightly) wrong by missing the fact that attackers are capable of strategically deciding to stop the attack in the middle of a batch (found by darosior).

Unit tests and fuzz tests are added, and at the end the old Python code is deleted.
</description>

[2026-10-25] c:6394267241 comment by fametrano (contributor):
tACK 0316d0dc9ec6a1abbe84489c44a47a2dd94c79ee

Compiled from this branch, the two new functions return the exact optimum of their model for all five chains, every six hours from 2026-10-25 to 2041. The same holds on a grid of heights from 1 to 5 million and clocks, some before genesis. The chosen bufsize always meets the attack budget. Summing the attack model term by term, in exact arithmetic, gives the closed form for every period up to 16 and bufsize up to 60. I checked this with a Python port and a brute-force search; I can share the scripts as a gist. The new unit tests and p2p_headers_sync_with_minchainwork.py pass, and the parameters its nodes log match the port at each node's clock.

At 2026-10-25 00:00 UTC the parameters, as period/bufsize, are mainnet 597/14697, testnet3 590/13096, testnet4 217/5604, signet 345/8770 and regtest 535/14517. Mainnet needs 689 KiB per peer against 722 KiB for the hard-coded 649/15400. On 2029-04-10, the date that pair was sized for, mainnet needs 14.7 KiB more than the pair, as you estimated. Testnet4 and signet fall much further, from 616/16199 and 629/15885, because each chain now uses its own genesis time, like HeadersSyncState's commitment bound when syncing from genesis. Rerunning the old script with 2009-01-03, mainnet's genesis date, reproduces all four hard-coded pairs.
</new_statements>
